To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
social relationships and social ties are important for health and well being because of the social support they provide.

the social ties and social support of individuals and the social networks of communities influence the health and well being of their members through the seven mechanisms described above and through stress buffering processes that also involve these seven mechanisms.

the beneficial effects of social relationships and social ties on health and well being are mediated by the mechanisms described above, which operate through the processes of social influence/social comparison; social control; role based purpose and mattering; self esteem; sense of control; belonging and companionship; and perceived support availability, and through stress buffering mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social context of stress and coping and the role of social relationships and social ties in promoting health and preventing disease.
how the nature of social relationships affects physical and mental health.
the mechanisms through which support and social ties improve health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

social relationships and social supports are important to physical and emotional health, and that these effects are mediated by the social mechanisms described above, but that the precise nature of these effects and the mechanisms involved remain to be fully understood.

social relationships and social ties have both direct and stress moderating influences on health and well being, and that these effects are mediated by social comparison, social control and role based purpose and self esteem, sense or control, belonging and social companionship, and support availability.

the mechanisms through which support improves health are: (1) the provision of emotional sustenance by significant others; (2) the provision of instrumental aid by significant others; and (3) the provision of empathy, active coping, and role modeling by similar others.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social relationships and support have beneficial impacts on physical and mental health, but the mechanisms by which these effects are achieved are complex and varied.
the mechanisms that link social relationships and support to health are not a simple set of linear pathways.
social ties, support, and stress buffering processes all operate through a variety of mechanisms to promote physical and mental well being.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social relationships and social ties are important for physical and psychological health because they provide a variety of social resources that can be used in times of stress and need.
social ties and support can improve health through multiple mechanisms, and the most efficacious types of social support are supplied by different types of supporters.

the social relationships that promote health do so by fostering a sense of mattering, self esteem, and belonging, and by providing emotional sustenance, active coping assistance and role modeling from significant others and experentially similar others.
